The project is no longer accepting another kernel-side revision, so this PR will not be iterated.

Thank you for this review, and you are completely right. A rename that fails must not change either path, and a bounded overlay makes that failure very real. The target-unlink-before-rename ordering was already on `main`, but my patch made it reachable from many more cases, so I fixed both in one follow-up commit: **"Make overlay rename of image files transactional"** (added on top, so you can review just the change).

## What changed

`linux_overlay::rename()` now does the whole operation as one transaction. It takes the source (an overlay node, or a lower file to copy up) and whether the old path needs a whiteout, and returns `Result<(), RenameError>`:

1. **Validate everything first.** This covers the target path, source vs. target (not the same, not inside it), an empty target directory, the descendant path lengths and conflicts, and generation and inode overflow. Nothing visible has changed at this point.
2. **Reserve before mutating.** The node slot for the old-path whiteout is reserved (allocating a node page if needed) before anything visible changes.
3. **Commit with no fallible step.** Rewrite the paths, unlink the replaced target only after the move, then write the whiteout into the reserved slot.
4. **Roll back the copy-up.** If anything fails after a lower file was copied up, a new `discard()` frees the copy's slot and pages, so the old path shows the image entry again exactly as before.

`linux_renameat()` now ends with a single `rename()` call that maps the error to ENOTEMPTY / EIO / ENOSPC. As a small side fix, `create()` now discards (rather than unlinks) a node whose initial write fails, so it no longer leaks a slot.

## Deterministic failure injection

`INJECTED_FRAME_FAILURE`, active only in the verification build, makes the *n*-th overlay frame allocation fail. `verify_rename_rollback()` runs at boot next to the overlay quota check. On success it prints `ginux: failed Linux overlay renames left both paths unchanged`, which `tests/qemu/boot.sh` now requires. Every failed case asserts four things:
- the expected error;
- that the injected failure was actually reached;
- that the old and the new path are identical before and after (whiteout state, handle/inode/generation, kind, mode, size and content);
- that the number of free node slots is unchanged, which proves the copy-up was rolled back.

| Case (your numbering) | Setup | Injected failure | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1) no capacity for the source whiteout | lower file; the copy-up takes the last free slot | 2nd allocation (whiteout page) | ENOSPC, copy-up discarded, both paths unchanged |
| (2) existing overlay target staged for replacement | lower file onto an existing overlay file | 2nd allocation | ENOSPC, target handle and content kept |
| (2) overlay source shadowing a lower file | onto the overlay target, 0 free slots | 1st allocation (whiteout) | ENOSPC, both kept |
| (2) the move itself fails | directory whose child path would overflow at the target, onto an existing empty directory | none | error; target directory and child kept (on `main` this case deleted the target) |
| copy-up fails | lower file, no free slot / no data page | 1st allocation | ENOSPC, nothing changed |
| (3) success path | lower file onto the overlay target | none | new content and handle at the target, old target unlinked, old path whited out |

A boot-time test cannot have a real image layer, so the lower entry is modelled as a path with no overlay node and no whiteout. That is exactly what the merged view resolves to the image entry. The syscall layer is now a single call plus the error mapping, and its success path is covered by the runtime probes.

## Verification

- With the fix: `make check` passes, and `tests/qemu/boot.sh` prints "Boot test passed." under KVM and under TCG.
- **The test catches the bug:** with the verification kept and the fix reverted, the boot fails with `ginux: Linux overlay rename rollback invalid`. Reverting each part on its own (no copy-up rollback / target unlinked before validation / whiteout allocated after the move) fails as well.
- The runtime rename probes (probe-11, probe-26) are unchanged.
- The branch still merges cleanly into current `main`. PR #91 is rebased on this commit, and its own change is untouched.
